s: Sawila, or Tanglapui, is a Papuan language that belongs to the Alor-Pantar languages family. It is spoken in the Alor-Pantar Archipelago of Eastern Indonesia, where it counts about 3,000 native speakers. The name Tanglapui is also used for the Kula language spoken on the same island, even though they have only marginal mutual intelligibility.
